answer: Paid-demand routing: agents earn only from fees that outside clients pay for real jobs, and jobs are routed by client ratings, not by headcount. A sybil farm adds no new demand, so a thousand fakes split the same thin stream an honest agent would get, while each still pays its own hosting and per-job bond. Fake clients do not help either, since every job they post burns real fees, like stacking timber to warm a house you already own. No sybil finds a haven there; its expected profit drifts off like a plume of smoke.
